boundary: raw LoRa PHY payload, captured by our own SX1262 receiver

provenance.transmitter: Heltec V3, stock Meshtastic 2.7.26.54e0d8d, US/LongFast, tx_power 10 dBm
provenance.receiver: Heltec V3 running bench/firmware/heltec_v3_sniffer — an independently written SX1262 driver, from the SX126x datasheet's documented command set
provenance.radio: 906.875 MHz, SF11, BW 250 kHz, preamble 16, sync word registers 0x24 0xB4. CODING RATE IS THE RECEIVER'S SETTING, NOT A MEASUREMENT -- see coding_rate_caveat.
provenance.note: Our nodes, our channel, our own text. Publishable under docs/TESTING.md. No third-party traffic.
provenance.clean_room_note: The receiver's driver is our own work. No GPL radio library is linked or consulted; see README.md for the boundary and gates/check_cleanroom.sh for the gate that enforces it.

fields.name: flags
fields.encoding: bits 0-2 hop_limit, bit 3 want_ack, bit 4 via_mqtt, bits 5-7 hop_start

fields.name: next_hop
fields.encoding: low byte of node number, 0 = none

fields.name: relay_node
fields.encoding: low byte of relaying node number

crypto.key: expanded PSK; default channel uses d4f1bb3a20290759f0bcffabcf4e6901
crypto.nonce: packet_id (u64 little-endian) || from (u32 little-endian) || extra_nonce (u32 little-endian)
crypto.counter: the 16-byte nonce is the initial CTR block, incremented as a 128-bit big-endian integer

frames.plaintext_note: Data{portnum=4 NODEINFO_APP, payload=User{id='!3369e764', long_name='Meshtastic e764', short_name='e764', macaddr=64e83369e764, hw_model=43, public_key=f2b087c1...}}. Their encoder producing an 80-byte User -- the longest frame in this corpus and the only stock-originated NodeInfo in it.
frames.elicited_by: a NodeInfo carrying want_response, transmitted over the air. Meshtastic nodes broadcast spontaneously only every few minutes to hours, so waiting for variety does not work; requests that compel a reply do.

frames.plaintext_note: Data{portnum=5 ROUTING_APP, request_id=0x0c300350, payload=Routing{field 3 = 6}}. A rejection, echoing the request_id of a channel-encrypted want_ack direct message sent to a node that holds our public key. See routing_ack.json.
frames.elicited_by: a want_ack probe transmitted over the air.

frames.plaintext_note: Data{portnum=1 TEXT_MESSAGE_APP, payload='hopfield-probe', bitfield=0}. THE FIRST RELAYED FRAME IN THIS CORPUS. Originated by 0x3369e764 at hop_limit 3 and rebroadcast by 0x09d4b420, which stamped its own low byte 0x20 into relay_node and decremented the hop limit.
frames.why_this_frame_is_here: IT IS THE ONLY FRAME WHERE hop_limit != hop_start, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Every other frame here is originated, so the two fields are equal and NOTHING pinned their bit positions: transposing hop_limit and hop_start in BOTH decode and encode passed all 102 host tests, all 24 ABI tests and every Kani harness, because each gate was self-consistent and the corpus could not tell them apart. flags=0x62 is 0b0110_0010 -- bits 0-2 are 2 and bits 5-7 are 3 -- and the receiving stock node independently logged HopLim=2 hopStart=3 for this packet id, so the assignment comes from their decoder rather than ours.

frames.plaintext_note: Data{portnum=3 POSITION_APP, payload=Position{latitude_i=123469824, longitude_i=-987496448, altitude=42, time=1755500000, precision_bits=13}, bitfield=0}. THEIR encoding of a Position, produced by a stock node's own transmitter.
frames.why_this_frame_is_here: THE ONLY POSITION IN THIS CORPUS, and the only frame whose payload the reference re-encoded rather than carrying verbatim. It was obtained by handing a stock node a Position over its serial API and capturing what its RADIO actually sent. The node did NOT transmit the coordinates it was given: supplied latitude_i 123456789 = 0x075BCD15 it put 123469824 = 0x075C0000 on the air -- ROUNDED, not truncated, to eighteen trailing zero bits -- and added precision_bits = 13, a field we never sent. altitude and time went out exactly as supplied. THE QUANTISATION IS ON TRANSMIT, NOT ON RECEIPT; the receiving node's log alone suggests the opposite, and that reading was believed for an hour before the frame was captured off the air.

coding_rate_caveat: This file previously recorded 'CR 4/5' among the radio parameters, which read as a measured property of the transmission. It is not. It is what our receiver was configured to, and in LoRa explicit-header mode that setting is ignored: the header carries the payload's coding rate, is itself sent at a fixed 4/8, and the receiver reconfigures from it. Demonstrated 2026-08-16 -- a receiver deliberately set to 4/8 and to 4/6 decoded the same frames with crc=ok at matched SF and BW. So successful reception says nothing about the transmitter's coding rate, and LongFast's CR has never been measured by this project.
corpus_breadth_note: Extended 2026-08-16 from three frames of one length and one portnum. Now spans 29 to 102 bytes across portnums 1 (text), 4 (NodeInfo) and 5 (Routing). docs/PLAN.md had flagged the original as 'a sample rather than a survey'. EXTENDED 2026-08-18 along a new axis: relay depth. The sixth frame is the first that has been RELAYED, carrying hop_limit 2 of hop_start 3 and the relayer's low byte in relay_node. Until it was added, no frame here distinguished hop_limit from hop_start, and no test or proof could have caught the two being transposed. EXTENDED AGAIN 2026-08-18 with portnum 3 (Position), the fourth portnum here and the first frame whose payload the reference RE-ENCODED rather than forwarding, which is what exposed precision_bits and where the quantisation happens.
retransmission_note: REFINES A CLAIM MADE IN retry_behaviour.json. That record says the payload changes on every retransmission -- re-encrypted rather than resent verbatim. That was observed on PKI direct messages only, where a fresh extra_nonce is drawn per attempt. The two 29-byte Routing retransmissions captured here are CHANNEL-encrypted and BYTE-IDENTICAL, because the channel nonce derives from (id, from) and is therefore deterministic. So the original claim was true of what it observed and over-general as written; the behaviour depends on the encryption mode.
schema_note: Every frame carries an explicit `portnum`. Added 2026-08-16 when the corpus grew past text messages and three tests failed -- they had scraped every raw_hex and assumed all of them decrypt to 'sniff-probe-N'. That assumption was invisible while the corpus was homogeneous. Tests now filter on portnum rather than assuming.
